description.summary: zero-copy, encoder-paced screen capture

protocol.description:
This protocol lets a privileged client receive the contents of an output as a continuous stream of frames, rendered by the compositor straight into GPU buffers the client allocated. It is designed for a hardware video encoder sitting directly behind it: frames are never copied through main memory, the compositor only produces a frame when something on screen changed (or when the client explicitly asks for one), and the rate at which frames are produced is set by how fast the client hands buffers back.
The model is a small ring of client-owned dmabuf buffers, attached once and reused for the lifetime of the session:
1. The client creates a session for an output. The compositor describes the buffers it can render into with a constraints / format / modifier / constraints_done sequence. 2. The client allocates up to four dmabuf wl_buffers that satisfy those constraints and attaches each to a ring slot with attach_buffer. Every slot starts out owned by the compositor. 3. The client calls start. From then on, whenever the captured content is damaged and a compositor-owned slot is available, the compositor renders the output into that slot and hands it to the client with damage events followed by a frame event. The slot then belongs to the client. 4. When the client is done with a slot (typically once the encoder has consumed it), it gives it back with release. Only released slots are ever rendered into again.
Ownership of a slot is therefore always unambiguous, and a client that holds every slot pauses capture without any extra request: the compositor simply has nowhere to render. That is the pacing mechanism — an encoder that falls behind is never overrun, and frames are never queued up behind it to add latency.
Synchronisation is implicit by default: a frame event is only sent once the GPU has finished rendering into the slot, and the client must not write to a slot after releasing it. A client that wants explicit synchronisation instead hands over two DRM syncobj timelines with set_timelines, one per direction: the compositor signals an acquire point on the acquire timeline for every frame, and the client signals a release point on the release timeline for every release (see set_timelines).
Only privileged clients can bind the manager global. A compositor must not expose it to sandboxed clients.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: crownos_screencast_manager_v1

description.summary: factory for screencast sessions

interface.description: A global factory for crownos_screencast_session_v1 objects, and the object that tells a client which optional features this compositor implements.

entry.name: invalid_cursor_mode
entry.summary: the cursor_mode argument is not a value of the cursor_mode enum

enum.name: cursor_mode

description.summary: how the pointer cursor is delivered

enum.description: Whether and how the pointer cursor appears in the captured stream.

entry.name: hidden
entry.summary: the cursor is neither drawn into frames nor reported

entry.name: embedded
entry.summary: the cursor is composited into every frame

entry.name: metadata
entry.summary: the cursor is left out of frames and reported with cursor events

enum.name: capability

description.summary: optional features of this compositor

enum.description: Optional features a compositor may or may not implement. A request that depends on a capability the compositor did not advertise raises the error named in that request's description.

entry.name: explicit_sync
entry.summary: set_timelines is supported

entry.name: toplevel_source
entry.summary: reserved for per-window capture; never advertised by version 1

request.name: destroy

description.summary: destroy the manager

request.description: Destroy the manager. Sessions created through it are unaffected and keep running until they are destroyed individually.

request.name: create_output_session

description.summary: capture an output

request.description:
Create a session capturing everything the compositor presents on the given output, in the output's own orientation: the frames are upright as the user sees them, whatever transform the output carries. Virtual outputs created with crownos-virtual-output-v1 are captured the same way.
The compositor sends the first constraints sequence immediately after this request is processed. If the output is not (or no longer) usable, the session is created anyway and immediately receives stopped(source_destroyed), so the client never needs to special-case a hotplug race.
Passing a cursor_mode that is not a value of the cursor_mode enum raises invalid_cursor_mode.
Capturing a single window is reserved for a future version, which will advertise the toplevel_source capability and add a create_toplevel_session request.

event.name: capabilities

description.summary: the optional features of this compositor

event.description: Sent once, immediately after the manager is bound. The set does not change for the lifetime of the manager object.

interface.name: crownos_screencast_session_v1

description.summary: one stream of frames from one source

interface.description:
A capture session: a source, a ring of up to four client-owned dmabuf buffers, and the stream of frames rendered into them.
A session moves through three phases. Before start, the client may attach buffers and set timelines, and the compositor renders nothing. After start, frames flow as described in the protocol description. After stopped, the session is inert: the compositor renders nothing and sends nothing more, every request other than destroy is ignored, and the client should destroy the object and free its buffers.
All buffer coordinates in this interface (damage, cursor position) are in pixels of the attached buffers, with the origin at the top-left corner of the captured image.

entry.name: invalid_index
entry.summary: the slot index is not smaller than the ring size

entry.name: already_attached
entry.summary: a buffer is already attached to this slot

entry.name: invalid_buffer
entry.summary: the buffer is not a dmabuf or does not satisfy the constraints

entry.name: already_started
entry.summary: start was sent more than once

entry.name: not_client_owned
entry.summary: release named a slot the client does not own

entry.name: timelines_exist
entry.summary: set_timelines was sent more than once

entry.name: sync_unsupported
entry.summary: set_timelines was sent without the explicit_sync capability

entry.name: invalid_timeline
entry.summary: a file descriptor is not a DRM syncobj the compositor can import

entry.name: late_timelines
entry.summary: set_timelines was sent after start

entry.name: invalid_release_point
entry.summary: a release point did not exceed the previous one of the session

entry.name: max_slots
entry.summary: the number of slots in the ring

entry.name: requested
entry.summary: the client sent stop

entry.name: source_destroyed
entry.summary: the captured output went away

entry.name: revoked
entry.summary: the compositor or the user withdrew permission to capture

entry.name: render_failed
entry.summary: the compositor could not render into the attached buffers

request.name: destroy

description.summary: end the session

request.description: Destroy the session. Rendering stops immediately. Buffers the compositor owned at that point are released by the compositor as if the session had stopped; the client may destroy them once this request has been sent.

request.name: attach_buffer

description.summary: put a buffer into a ring slot

request.description:
Attach a dmabuf-backed wl_buffer to ring slot index. The slot becomes compositor-owned: the compositor may render into it at any time after start, and the client must neither read nor write the buffer until it is handed back with a frame event.
A slot is attached once and stays attached for the life of the session, with one exception: every constraints sequence after the first empties every slot (see constraints), after which each slot can be attached again.
The buffer must have been created through zwp_linux_dmabuf_v1 and its size, format and modifier must be one of the combinations the latest constraints sequence advertised; otherwise invalid_buffer is raised. index must be smaller than max_slots, or invalid_index is raised. Attaching to a slot that already holds a buffer raises already_attached.
The client keeps ownership of the wl_buffer object and must not destroy it while it is attached; destroying an attached buffer makes the session stop with render_failed.

request.name: set_timelines

description.summary: switch the session to explicit synchronisation

request.description:
Import two DRM timeline syncobjs, each exported with drmSyncobjHandleToFD, and use them for every frame and release of this session. They must be two distinct syncobjs: signalling a point of a timeline implies that every lower point is signalled too, so the two parties can only share a timeline if they agree on one order of signalling, which frames and releases do not have.
The acquire timeline is signalled by the compositor only: - every frame event names an acquire point on it. Acquire points start above zero, strictly increase with every frame event of the session, and are signalled in increasing order, each once the GPU has finished rendering the frame that names it. - the compositor may send a frame event before rendering has finished; the client must wait for the frame's acquire point before reading the slot. The client must never signal this timeline.
The release timeline is signalled by the client only: - every release names a release point on it, which must be above zero and above the release point of every earlier release of the session, or invalid_release_point is raised. - the client signals its release points in increasing order, from the CPU or from GPU work, once it no longer reads the slot. The compositor waits for the point to be signalled before rendering into the slot again, so the client may release a slot as soon as it has queued the GPU work that reads it, without waiting for that work to finish. Since the timeline is ordered, signalling a point also returns every slot released with a lower point. The compositor never signals this timeline.
Without timelines, a frame event is sent only once rendering into the slot has completed, the acquire point arguments of frame are zero, and the release point arguments of release are ignored: a slot may be rendered into again as soon as it is released. A session therefore synchronises either explicitly in both directions or implicitly in both; there is no mixed mode.
This request is only valid before start (late_timelines), at most once (timelines_exist), and only if the manager advertised the explicit_sync capability (sync_unsupported). A descriptor the compositor cannot import raises invalid_timeline.

arg.name: acquire_timeline
arg.summary: DRM syncobj the compositor signals frames on

arg.name: release_timeline
arg.summary: DRM syncobj the client signals releases on

request.name: start

description.summary: begin producing frames

request.description:
Start capture. The first frame is rendered as soon as a compositor-owned slot is available, whether or not anything was damaged, so the client always receives a complete image first.
max_fps_mhz caps the frame rate, in millihertz: 30000 means at most 30 frames per second. Zero means no cap beyond the source's own refresh. The cap is an upper bound, not a promise: the compositor only renders into a slot whose contents are out of date with the source, so a static source produces no frames once every slot has caught up, unless force_frame asks for one.
Sending start more than once raises already_started.

arg.name: max_fps_mhz
arg.summary: frame rate cap in mHz, 0 for none

request.name: release

description.summary: give a slot back to the compositor

request.description:
Hand slot index back to the compositor, which may render into it again. With timelines set, release_point is a point on the release timeline that the compositor waits for and that must exceed every earlier release point of the session (see set_timelines); without timelines it is ignored and should be zero.
The slot must be client-owned, i.e. handed out by a frame event and not released since; otherwise not_client_owned is raised. Releasing a slot that was emptied by a constraints change is not an error and has no effect, because the client cannot have known.

arg.name: release_point_hi
arg.summary: high 32 bits of the release point

arg.name: release_point_lo
arg.summary: low 32 bits of the release point

request.name: force_frame

description.summary: ask for one complete frame

request.description:
Render the next frame in full, even if nothing was damaged, and report the whole buffer as damaged. Meant for answering a keyframe request from a decoder while the screen is static.
The forced frame is produced as soon as a compositor-owned slot is available and the frame rate cap allows; several force_frame requests before that happens produce a single frame. Before start, the request is remembered for the first frame, which is complete anyway.

request.name: stop

description.summary: stop producing frames

request.description: Stop capture. The compositor answers with stopped(requested); frames rendered before that remain valid and client-owned. Sending stop on a session that is already stopped has no effect.

event.name: constraints

description.summary: the buffers the compositor can render into

event.description:
Begins a constraints sequence: this event, then one format event per pixel format with the modifier events for that format, then constraints_done. The sequence as a whole replaces any previous one.
width and height are the size, in pixels, that attached buffers must have. They follow the source: a mode or scale change of the output produces a new sequence.
Every sequence after the first empties the ring. Every slot, whoever owns it, is detached; the compositor stops rendering until buffers satisfying the new constraints are attached, and frames resume from there with a complete image, as after start. Frames the client already holds remain readable but can no longer be released.

event.name: format

description.summary: a pixel format the compositor can render into

event.description:
A DRM fourcc code (see drm_fourcc.h) the compositor can render this source into. Always followed by at least one modifier event for it.
Besides RGB formats, a compositor that can convert colour on the GPU advertises NV12 (DRM_FORMAT_NV12). NV12 frames hold BT.709 limited-range YCbCr, with chroma sited at the centre of each 2x2 block, so they can be handed to a video encoder without any conversion on the client side.

event.name: modifier

description.summary: a layout modifier for an advertised format

event.description: A DRM format modifier the compositor can render format into. The modifier is split into two 32-bit halves. format is always one announced by a preceding format event of the same sequence.

event.name: constraints_done

description.summary: the constraints sequence is complete

event.description: Ends a constraints sequence. The client can now allocate and attach buffers that match it.

event.name: damage

description.summary: a region that changed

event.description: A rectangle, in buffer coordinates, whose contents differ from the previous frame event of this session. Any number of damage events precede each frame event and apply to it; their union may be larger than what actually changed, but never smaller. The first frame after start, after a constraints change and after force_frame is always damaged in full.

event.name: frame

description.summary: a slot now holds a new frame

event.description:
Slot index holds a new frame and now belongs to the client until it is released. The damage events sent since the previous frame event describe what changed.
The timestamp is the CLOCK_MONOTONIC time at which the frame's content was sampled, the same clock wp_presentation reports, split into seconds (hi and lo 32 bits) and nanoseconds.
acquire_point is the point on the acquire timeline to wait on before reading the slot when timelines were set (see set_timelines), and zero otherwise.

arg.name: acquire_point_hi
arg.summary: high 32 bits of the acquire point

arg.name: acquire_point_lo
arg.summary: low 32 bits of the acquire point

event.name: cursor_position

description.summary: where the cursor is on the captured image

event.description:
Only sent in metadata cursor mode. The pointer's hot point moved to x, y in buffer coordinates. hotspot_x and hotspot_y repeat the current shape's hot point, so the top-left corner of the cursor image is at (x - hotspot_x, y - hotspot_y). The position may lie partly outside the buffer while the cursor straddles the output's edge.
Sent whenever the cursor moves over the captured output, independently of frame events: moving the cursor in metadata mode damages nothing.

arg.name: hotspot_x
arg.summary: hot point x within the cursor image

arg.name: hotspot_y
arg.summary: hot point y within the cursor image

event.name: cursor_leave

description.summary: the cursor left the captured image

event.description: Only sent in metadata cursor mode. The pointer is no longer over the captured output; the client should stop drawing it until the next cursor_position event.

event.name: cursor_buffer

description.summary: pixels of the next cursor shape

event.description: Only sent in metadata cursor mode, and always immediately before the cursor_shape event it belongs to. fd is a sealed, read-only memory file holding the image as premultiplied ARGB8888 (little-endian, as DRM_FORMAT_ARGB8888), stride bytes per row, already scaled to buffer pixels. The client may map it and must close it.

arg.name: fd
arg.summary: sealed memory file with the pixels

event.name: cursor_shape

description.summary: the cursor changed shape

event.description:
Only sent in metadata cursor mode, and only when the shape actually changes. If a cursor_buffer event immediately preceded this one, its pixels are the new shape; otherwise the cursor has no image (a client hid it) and nothing should be drawn until the next cursor_shape.
serial increases with every shape change of the session. hotspot_x and hotspot_y are the hot point within the image, in buffer pixels.

event.name: stopped

description.summary: the session ended

event.description: The session stopped and will produce nothing more. Slots the client owns stay readable; the client should destroy the session and then its buffers. This is the last event sent on the object.
